Estimate within-cell residual variances from a coded pilot sample

Source: R/pilot_functions.R
estimate_pilot_variances.Rd

Computes, for each treatment-by-stratum cell, the pilot sample size, mean residual, and residual variance, and returns them in the format calc_optimal_allocation expects for var_alloc. Cells with fewer than min_pilot pilot units (or an inestimable variance) fall back to the pooled within-arm pilot variance, with a warning. Optionally, cell means and variances can be empirical-Bayes shrunk toward pooled, within-arm values.

estimate_pilot_variances(
  dat,
  S = "S_pilot",
  Z = NULL,
  strata = "strata",
  Yobs = "Yobs",
  Yhat = "Yhat",
  min_pilot = 2,
  shrink = TRUE
)

Arguments

dat

Data frame

S

Name of (or vector for) the 0/1 pilot indicator. Pilot units must have non-missing Yobs.

Z

Name of treatment indicator column, or NULL.

strata

Name of stratification column, or NULL for one stratum.

Yobs, Yhat

Names of observed/predicted outcome columns.

min_pilot

Minimum pilot units per cell before falling back to the pooled variance. Default 2.

shrink

Logical. If FALSE (default), var.alloc and mean.alloc are just the raw per-cell values (with the min_pilot fallback applied to var.alloc, as before). If TRUE, both are empirical-Bayes shrunk, in two stages, with variances pooled fully across treatment arms and means handled as a "hybrid": variances are shrunk first, toward a single pooled variance computed across all cells regardless of arm (a Smyth (2004)-style, df-weighted posterior mean) – variances are a harder-to-estimate, second-order concern here, so all cells are pooled for maximum stability. Those shrunk variances are then used, in place of the raw variances, to shrink the cell means (a DerSimonian-Laird-style Fay-Herriot/James-Stein estimator): the amount of shrinkage (the between-cell variance sigma^2_u) is likewise estimated once across all cells, but each cell is shrunk toward its own arm's precision-weighted grand mean, not a single grand mean pooled across arms, since arms may carry a genuine mean-residual shift. See scripts/pilot_shrinkage_memo.md for the derivation and citations.

Value

Data frame with one row per cell: .Z, .strata, N.zk, n_pilot.zk, mean_resid_pilot (raw), var_resid_pilot (raw), var_pooled, var.alloc, and mean.alloc. When shrink = FALSE, var.alloc and mean.alloc equal the raw per-cell values (subject to the min_pilot fallback on var.alloc); when shrink = TRUE they are the shrunk values described above.
